card.statement:
For any $\mu\in\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$ we have a canonical isomorphism

$(r_{\mu})^{*}\mathrm{IC}_{\overline{\mathrm{Bun}}_{U}}[\langle\mu,2\rho\rangle-(g-1)\dim(U)]\cong\mathrm{IC}_{\overline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}}.$

In [17] it is assumed that $\Bbbk$ has characteristic $0$, but the same proof applies in general. (The author also uses $!$ -pullback instead of $*$ -pullback, but the two versions are equivalent by Grothendieck–Verdier duality.) Namely, in case $\mu$ satisfies $\langle\mu,\alpha\rangle>2g-2$ for any positive root $\alpha$, the morphism $r_{\mu}$ is smooth by Remark 4.12. Since $\overline{\mathrm{Bun}}_{U}$ has dimension $(g-1)\dim(U)$ and $\overline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}$ has dimension $\langle\mu,2\rho\rangle$, the formula of the proposition follows from a classical property of smooth pullback. The proof in general proceeds by reduction to this case using factorization; see [17, §3.9] for details.

4.10. Central fiber

Recall from (2.9) that the closed stratum in the stratification (2.8) (corresponding to $\Gamma=[\mu]$ ) identifies with $C$. We set

$\mathbf{F}^{\mu}:=C\times_{C^{\mu}}\mathbf{Z}^{\mu},$

where the morphism $C\to C^{\mu}$ is the embedding of that stratum. (This is a stack over $C\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}$.) We also set

$\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}}\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}=\{\mathcal{F}^{0}\}\times_{\mathrm{Bun}_{T}}\mathbf{F}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}}\mathbf{Z}^{\mu}$

(where in the right-hand side, the map $C\to C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}$ is given by $E\mapsto(\mu\cdot E,\mathcal{F}^{0})$ ) and

$\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}}\overline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}=C\times_{C\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}}\mathbf{F}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}^{-\mu}}\mathbf{Z}^{\mu}$

(where in the third term the map $C\to C\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}$ is given by $E\mapsto(E,\mathcal{F}^{0}(\mu\cdot E))$, and in the right-hand side the map $C\to C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}^{-\mu}$ is given by $E\mapsto(\mu\cdot E,\mathcal{F}^{0}(\mu\cdot E))$ ). These are schemes over $C$. The decompositions (4.24) induce decompositions

$\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=\bigsqcup_{0\preceq\nu\preceq\mu}{}_{\nu}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}\quad\text{where ${}_{\nu}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}}{}_{\nu}\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}\cong{}_{0}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu-\nu}$}$

and

$\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=\bigsqcup_{0\preceq\nu\preceq\mu}{}_{\nu}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}\quad\text{where ${}_{\nu}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}=C\times_{C^{\mu}}{}_{\nu}\overline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}$.}$

Given a closed point $c\in C$, we set

$\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}=\{c\}\times_{C}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu},\quad\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}=\{c\}\times_{C}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}.$

If $\nu$ satisfies $0\preceq\nu\preceq\mu$, we also set

${}_{\nu}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}=\{c\}\times_{C}{}_{\nu}\underline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu},\quad{}_{\nu}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu,c}=\{c\}\times_{C}{}_{\nu}\overline{\mathbf{F}}^{\mu}.$
card.label: Proposition 4.16

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
